Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I’ve summarized the pragmatic tradeoffs below and attached a one-page cheat sheet for your procurement team. Short answer: if speed-to-PO is the priority, go Private Offer (AWS) / Azure Private Offers or GCP Marketplace private pricing — we can be seller-of-record and accept a PO depending on the marketplace's invoicing flow. If you need custom commercial terms (data residency, indemnity edits), a direct MSA will be faster for negotiable redlines.

High-level pros/cons (practical lens):
- Marketplace Private Offer (AWS/Azure/GCP):
  - Pros: Often shortest procurement path (PO via cloud provider, private offers expedite procurement), can enable seller-of-record in many cases, simpler onboarding for cloud-native finance teams, easier co-sell tracking with cloud partner teams.
  - Cons: Some marketplace billing paths route through the cloud provider (affects revenue recognition/co-sell crediting timing); certain contract clauses (custom indemnities/SLAs) are limited.

- Direct MSA (signed with Redwood):
  - Pros: Full control over contract language, Redwood is clearly seller-of-record, direct invoicing from Redwood to FinHealth, simpler for long-term billing relationships and custom terms.
  - Cons: Negotiation can take longer; procurement teams sometimes require additional approvals vs. private offers.

Operational notes that matter for procurement and PO flows:
- Seller-of-record: We can be seller-of-record on a private offer depending on the cloud provider and the configuration (we’ve done this with several enterprise pilots). If seller-of-record is a hard requirement, we’ll validate per-cloud — AWS Private Offers can support it, Azure has marketplace models with partner billing options, and GCP offers purchase orders via partner resellers.
- Invoicing cadence: Marketplaces often bill via the cloud provider monthly and send a consolidated invoice; direct MSA lets us invoice on your cadence and apply PO numbers directly on Redwood invoices.
- Co-sell credits & partner motions: If you want to leverage co-sell incentives, the cloud marketplace listing + a registered partner motion is the usual path; we’ll coordinate our partner rep to make sure credits flow to the right team. However, co-sell credits can lag and are subject to the cloud partner’s rules.
- Security evidence: attaching a SOC 2 snapshot now (redacted). We can also complete your procurement questionnaire and return it in 48–72 business hours.

Recommendation for a 50–100 dev pilot (goal = fast procurement + clean PO integration):
1) Start with a Private Offer (AWS or Azure private pricing) configured so Redwood can accept the PO and act as seller-of-record. This usually clears procurement in 1–2 weeks once the private offer is issued.
2) If Procurement requires contract edits (custom SLAs or data residency clauses), run a narrow direct MSA in parallel — we’ll prioritize legal redlines to keep timing tight.
3) We’ll prepare a lightweight mutual action plan (attached) with milestones and acceptance criteria so both sides have a clear timeline.

Next steps I can take this week:
- Validate seller-of-record settings with our marketplace ops contacts for AWS/Azure/GCP (I’ll ping them and report back by Thu EOD).
- Fill out and return your procurement questionnaire (we’ll return a completed PDF + SOC2 snapshot).
- If you want to move via Private Offer, confirm preferred cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) and your PO number format.
